summary: Iteration 3 backend-only testing of Portail ALBARKA. Added /app/backend/tests/test_iteration3.py (39 new tests) covering: the seeded Admin@sawalismartsystems.com account (login + OTP -> roles ['direction','superviseur']), admin settings GET/PUT/RBAC + masking of wa_access_token, WhatsApp Meta Cloud API guarding (wa/test with wa_enabled=false -> {ok:false,message_id:null}), report numbering PREFIX-CLIENT-TYPE-YYYYMM-NNNN with per-client/per-type/per-month sequences, report list (sort desc + month_key/kind filters), PDF download (headers + parsed content containing number/kind/period), send-by-email with base64 PDF attachment, sign/double-sign/delete rules, tenant isolation on list/download/sign/delete, notify_upload firing on client uploads (confirmed in backend logs: emails attempted to superviseur, comptable and admin), the can_receive_notifications gate on notify_echeance and the Mongo staff filter, and the can_receive_notifications field on client create/patch. Full suite result: 130 tests, 129 passing. The single failure (TestEmailTransport::test_notify_echeance_skips_whatsapp_silently) is the Emergent Resend proxy returning HTTP 429 'email rate limit exceeded' because the suite itself (notify_upload fans out one email per staff member on every upload + cron trigger + 2 transport tests + report send) exceeds the proxy quota; the same call succeeds after the quota window resets (verified 202 + message id). Report send WITH the base64 PDF attachment works (returns a real Resend message id and persists email_sent_at/email_sent_to). Two stale iteration-2 assertions were updated (PDF header text changed; dedup row is now only written on successful send, so a failed send is retried - I added a positive dedup test instead). Two genuine defects found: (1) report numbers collide across different clients whose names share the first 7 letters (proved: two clients both got RAP-SAWADOG-MENSUEL-203201-0001); (2) the iteration-2 CRITICAL cron auth mismatch is still unfixed - crons.yml has no Authorization header and POST /api/cron/notify-echeances without a header still returns 401.

critical.issue: Report numbers are NOT unique across clients. _client_slug() takes only the first 7 alphabetic chars of full_name while the counter is keyed on tenant_id, so two distinct clients whose names share those 7 letters produce the exact same number. Reproduced: clients 'Sawadogo Alpha QA' and 'Sawadogo Beta QA' both received 'RAP-SAWADOG-MENSUEL-203201-0001'. For an accounting deliverable this is a compliance problem. Fix: include a per-client stable discriminator (client code / short id) in the slug, or add a unique index on client_reports.number and retry on collision.

STILL UNFIXED from iteration 2. crons.yml declares no headers, but the endpoint requires 'Authorization: Bearer <WEBHOOK_CRON_SECRET>'. Re-verified now: POST without header -> 401 {'detail':'Auth manquante'}. The 07:00 UTC job will 401 forever and no reminder will ever be sent in production.

minor.issue: This endpoint re-implements the Resend proxy call inline instead of reusing albarka_notifications.send_email, so the email guardrails (_assert_safe_email: no forms, no credential asks, https-only links, anchor-host match) are BYPASSED for report emails. Route the payload through a shared helper that runs the guardrails and adds the attachment.

Fans out one sequential Resend call per staff member on every single upload, with no batching, no 429 handling and no retry (errors are swallowed by send_email). This is what tripped the proxy's 'email rate limit exceeded' (429) during the suite. Use one message with multiple recipients/BCC, or a queue with backoff.

Deletes only the Mongo document; the archived PDF at albarka/{tenant}/reports/{month}/{number}.pdf is left orphaned in R2/local storage forever. Also the report_series counter is not decremented (acceptable) so numbers are consumed by deleted drafts.

Returns {ok:false, message_id:null} with no reason. An admin cannot distinguish 'wa_enabled=false', 'missing token/phone id' and 'Meta rejected the token' - all three paths return the same body while the real error is only in the server log. Return a short diagnostic message.

report_prefix has only max_length=10 and no pattern; setting 'rap 1' or 'r@p' produces numbers that no longer match the documented ^RAP-[A-Z]+-... contract. Validate with pattern ^[A-Z]{2,10}$ (and uppercase it).

Since build_client_report_pdf gained header_number/report_kind_label/month_key, the legacy route passes none of them, so the produced PDF now has no title/type at all in its header (only 'CABINET ALBARKA' + client name). Either pass a label or drop the legacy route in favour of /reports/client/{id}/generate.

server.py creates indexes for cron_runs, notification_log, echeances, users, otps and documents but none for the new collections: no index on client_reports (tenant_id, generated_at) or client_reports.id, and no UNIQUE index on report_series.key - the find_one_and_update upsert is atomic per document but a race can still create two series docs for the same key without the unique constraint.
Hard 500-item cap with no pagination and no total count; month_key/kind are not validated (an unknown kind silently returns [] instead of 400).

The admin email is stored lowercased ('admin@sawalismartsystems.com') while the docs/credentials show 'Admin@sawalismartsystems.com'. Login is case-insensitive so this is cosmetic, but any code doing an exact-match lookup on the documented casing will miss the account.

action_items: CRITICAL: make report numbers unique per client (slug collision proved) - add a client code to the slug and/or a unique index on client_reports.number.

CRITICAL (carried over from iteration 2): add the Authorization: Bearer <WEBHOOK_CRON_SECRET> header in /app/.emergent/crons.yml, or accept the platform cron auth - /api/cron/notify-echeances still 401s without it.
Route /reports/{id}/send through albarka_notifications so the email guardrails run; support attachments in that shared helper.
Batch notify_upload into a single multi-recipient email and handle the proxy's 429 (rate limit was hit during testing).
Delete the stored PDF object when a report is deleted.
Return a diagnostic message from /admin/settings/wa/test and validate report_prefix with ^[A-Z]{2,10}$.
Add indexes: client_reports (tenant_id, generated_at) + unique report_series.key; add pagination to the report list.
critical_code_review_comments: albarka_reports_mgmt._client_slug: derives the human part of a legally-referenced number from a truncated name; combined with a per-tenant counter this yields duplicate numbers for similarly named clients. Numbering must be provably unique (unique index + retry).

albarka_reports_mgmt.send_report_email duplicates ~40 lines of Resend transport already present in albarka_notifications.send_email and skips _assert_safe_email - a DRY and a safety-guardrail violation at once.

albarka_admin_settings imports get_current_user but never uses it; also _load_settings performs a write ($set of every default key) on a GET path whenever a new default key appears - fine once, but it makes GET /admin/settings non-idempotent on deploy.

albarka_documents uses bare asyncio.create_task for notify_upload and for _analyze_and_store with no reference kept and no exception handler; tasks can be GC'd mid-flight and failures are only visible in logs. Prefer FastAPI BackgroundTasks or a task set with a done-callback.
No index exists for the new client_reports/report_series collections while /reports/client/{id}/list sorts on generated_at - an unindexed collection scan on Atlas.

send_email swallows every exception and returns None, so callers (notify_upload, cron) cannot distinguish 'not configured' from 429 rate-limited from 422 undeliverable; this hid the rate-limit condition until logs were read.

success_rate.backend: 99% (129/130 pytest tests passing; the single failure is the Resend proxy 429 rate limit, not application logic)

Please add the admin row to test_credentials.md.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite layout: /app/backend/tests/{conftest.py,backend_test.py,test_rbac_edge.py,test_reports_notifications.py,test_iteration3.py}; run with `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -q` (pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope). conftest exposes make_session/login_full and superviseur/comptable/client1/client2 fixtures; test_iteration3 adds an `admin` session fixture and a `mongo` fixture (pymongo on MONGO_URL/DB_NAME from backend/.env) used for direct DB assertions (masked-token persistence, email_sent_at, un-signing a report before delete). IMPORTANT: the Emergent Resend proxy is rate-limited - running the whole suite twice back-to-back WILL produce 429s and email-dependent tests (TestEmailTransport, TestReportSendSignDelete::test_send_report_email) will fail spuriously; wait ~4 minutes between full runs. Seeded @albarka-demo.bf recipients always 422 (undeliverable_recipient) - use delivered@resend.dev. I also saw one transient Cloudflare 502 HTML page from the ingress on /reports/{id}/send while the proxy was rate-limiting; it passed on retry, so treat a lone 502 there as flaky and re-run. Reports use future months (2031-*) to keep numbering deterministic - delete the report_series rows for those months if you re-run number-sequence assertions. Frontend has never been exercised in any iteration: the admin settings screen, report list/month filter/send button and signature UI all still need a pass.
rca_of_the_issue: Number collision RCA: generate_report builds the number as f"{prefix}-{_client_slug(full_name)}-{KIND}-{YYYYMM}-{seq:04d}" where _client_slug strips non-alpha chars and truncates to 7, while _next_number keys the counter on tenant_id. Two different tenants therefore keep independent counters that both start at 1 while producing an identical visible slug - so the emitted numbers are identical strings, and nothing (no unique index on client_reports.number) detects it. Email 429 RCA: albarka_notifications.notify_upload loops over every active staff member and awaits a separate POST to the Emergent Resend proxy per recipient; combined with the cron trigger and the two transport tests, a single suite run issues well over a dozen sends in ~80s and the proxy answers 429 'email rate limit exceeded'. send_email's broad except returns None, so the caller reports sent_email=False with no distinction from a configuration problem, which is why the failure surfaced as an opaque assertion error rather than a rate-limit signal.
